channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Armenia Loses Voting Rights in CSTO Due to Unfulfilled Obligations
item.description: Member states of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) have decided to suspend Armenia's voting rights within the organization. Armenia will also be unable to appoint representatives to responsible positions within the CSTO. This decision stems from Armenia's failure to fulfill its obligations for several years, according to Dmitry Peskov, the press secretary of the Russian president.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Boost Cooperation in Digital Economy and Advanced Technologies
item.description: During a visit to Seoul, Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson met with the Speaker of South Korea's National Assembly. They praised the growing inter-parliamentary ties and agreed to enhance collaboration in artificial intelligence, critical minerals, digital economy, and advanced technologies. Discussions also covered education, healthcare, culture, and humanitarian activities.

item.title: Tokayev Attends CSTO Collective Security Council Meeting in Moscow
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev participated in the Collective Security Council meeting of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) in Moscow. Leaders discussed key aspects of cooperation, assessed the organization's performance, and outlined future work. They also exchanged views on international and regional security issues.

item.title: Gaza Health Ministry Reports Eight Palestinians Killed in Last 24 Hours
item.description: The Gaza Health Ministry announced that at least eight Palestinians were killed and 29 injured in the past 24 hours. Since the ceasefire in October last year, 1,622 Palestinians have been killed and 5,878 injured. The ministry stated that since the war began in October 2023, 74,653 Palestinians have been killed and 176,007 injured.

item.title: Uzbek First Lady Meets French President Macron in Paris
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with Emmanuel Macron in Paris. Discussions focused on developing cooperation between Uzbekistan and France in defense, security, cyber technologies, artificial intelligence, and economic and humanitarian spheres.

item.title: Central Asian Nations and Azerbaijan Plan Unified Payment System
item.description: Central Asian countries and Azerbaijan have agreed in principle to integrate instant payment systems. A joint working group will seek a model for QR-code payments via familiar banking apps for citizens traveling between these republics. The initiative aims to boost trade and tourism.

item.title: Young Athlete Fatally Stabbed in Takhar Province
item.description: A young athlete, identified as Enayatullah and a member of Takhar Province's karate team, was fatally stabbed in Rustaq district. The incident occurred near a Taliban district police headquarters. The motive behind the killing remains unclear amid rising insecurity in the region.

item.title: UN Reports Over 1,000 Afghans Returning Daily from Iran Amid Crisis
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that approximately 1,500 Afghan citizens are returning daily from Iran to Afghanistan via the Pul-e Abrisham/Milak border crossing. Many require urgent medical care due to injuries sustained on difficult journeys. This influx occurs as Afghanistan faces severe economic and social crises, compounded by falling temperatures.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Finland Leaders Discuss Cooperation Prospects at COP29
item.description: The leaders of Uzbekistan and Finland, Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Alexander Stubb, met on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya. They discussed implementing agreements from Stubb's previous visit to Uzbekistan, focusing on increasing trade, joint projects in metallurgy, energy, geology, ecology, and water resources. A business forum and intergovernmental commission meeting are planned for early 2027.

item.title: Iran: Enriched uranium will not be exported, says security chief
item.description: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, reiterated Tehran's stance that enriched uranium will not be transferred to another country as part of any potential nuclear deal with the U.S. Rezaei stated Iran will not remove "a single atom" of its enriched nuclear material and that Moscow has been informed. Russia has been frequently mentioned as a potential location for Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpiles.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan ready to host CSTO joint military exercises in 2027
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced Kyrgyzstan's readiness to host Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) joint military exercises in 2027. Speaking at a CSTO session in Moscow, Japarov highlighted Kyrgyzstan's commitment to collective security and practical cooperation within the alliance. He emphasized the importance of such events for enhancing combat readiness and coordination among collective forces.

item.title: Japan seeks deeper economic partnership with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Japan's Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, Ryuichi Hirano, expressed Japan's intention to deepen economic ties with Kyrgyzstan, moving towards a broader economic partnership. He noted Kyrgyzstan's growing economic and diplomatic influence, citing its upcoming non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council. The ambassador highlighted the solid foundation for mutually beneficial cooperation, building on recent high-level meetings and a joint statement on relations.

item.title: Russian region expands list of professions banned for migrant workers
item.description: The Saratov region in Russia will expand the list of professions banned for migrant workers starting January 1, 2027. Migrants working under patents will be prohibited from working in energy, water supply, and freight transport sectors. This adds to existing restrictions in services, education, and healthcare.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Student faces charges for false terrorism report
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Pavlodar, Kazakhstan, against a teenager who made a false report about a planned terrorist act. The youth called emergency services after finding an unattended phone in a gym, unaware of the consequences. Authorities are reminding the public that false reports carry up to five years imprisonment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aviation Authority discusses measures against bird strikes
item.description: The Civil Aviation Committee of Kazakhstan held a meeting with Air Astana representatives to discuss ornithological safety in airports. Air Astana presented data on bird strike incidents and challenges. Both parties agreed on the need for regular collaboration between regulators, airlines, and airport services to mitigate risks.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Continue Preparations for Free Trade Agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are actively working to expand trade turnover and finalize a free trade agreement, according to the Senate press service. Discussions included promoting Uzbek agricultural products in Korea, supporting local exporters, and establishing joint ventures. Both sides emphasized the importance of consultations between relevant ministries and agencies.

item.title: Uzbek President and World Bank Head Discuss Strategic Partnership Priorities
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with World Bank Group President Ajay Banga to discuss expanding strategic partnership. The joint project portfolio has reached nearly $16 billion. Priorities include implementing the Growth and Jobs Program, preparing a new Country Partnership Strategy, attracting private investment in infrastructure, and ensuring water security.

item.title: Uzbekistan Customs Briefly Suspends Phone Clearance Over IMEI Issues, Resumes Operations
item.description: Tashkent airport customs temporarily halted the clearance of imported mobile phones on November 10 due to IMEI registration concerns. The procedure resumed less than 24 hours later, with the Customs Committee stating clarity had been restored. Passengers had previously complained about lengthy "expertises" and high fees for expedited processing.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Propose UN Resolution on Child Welfare Based on Samarkand Declaration
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to submit a draft resolution to the UN General Assembly based on the Samarkand Declaration on Investing in Child Well-being. Saida Mirziyoyeva announced this at the Paris Peace Forum, emphasizing the need for real international impact for children's promises. The declaration aims to progressively increase state investments in child health, education, and social protection.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov Addresses CSTO Security Council Meeting in Moscow
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov spoke at the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) Security Council session in Moscow. He highlighted Russia's significant work during its CSTO presidency and emphasized Kyrgyzstan's commitment to strengthening collective security and developing practical cooperation among member states. Japarov also noted Kyrgyzstan's readiness to host joint CSTO events in 2027.

item.title: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Warns of Terrorism Threat from Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's foreign minister stated that terrorism originating in Afghanistan remains a significant threat to Pakistan. He called for measures to prevent militants from utilizing Afghan territory to launch attacks against neighboring countries, highlighting the ongoing security concerns.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UNDP Cooperation Exceeds $550 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's cooperation with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has surpassed $550 million. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo to discuss expanding cooperation in sustainable development and climate change adaptation. Over 100 projects worth over $120 million have been implemented in the last five years.

item.title: Pakistan highlights terrorism from Afghanistan as major security concern
item.description: Pakistan's foreign minister stated that terrorism originating from Afghanistan remains a significant security challenge for Pakistan. He urged for measures to prevent militants from using Afghan territory to launch attacks on neighboring countries. Pakistan accuses the Taliban of harboring the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, which has claimed responsibility for attacks within Pakistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan opens mudslide and landslide monitoring post in Turkestan region
item.description: A monitoring post for mudslides and landslides has been opened in the Kazygurt district of Kazakhstan's Turkestan region. The facility will provide round-the-clock surveillance of natural threats. The area has 34 zones prone to mudslides, landslides, and avalanches, affecting over 1,500 residents and 426 structures. The post was funded by the Kazakhstan Rescuers Fund.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UN Agree to Expand Programs Combating Desertification and Restoring Aral Sea Region
item.description: Uzbekistan and the UN have agreed to enhance cooperation on combating land degradation, desertification, and climate change adaptation. The partnership has successfully implemented 15 joint projects in the past five years. Discussions focused on ecological recovery of the Aral Sea region, increasing protective forests, and carbon sequestration.

item.title: US Envoys to Meet Presidents Putin and Zelenskyy Amidst Ukraine Conflict
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and later report to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin. These meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at de-escalating the conflict in Ukraine, which included discussions on a potential large-scale prisoner exchange.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Strengthen Cooperation in Immunization Programs
item.description: Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan are enhancing their collaboration on immunization. A three-day working visit by a Kazakh delegation concluded, involving health ministries and WHO country offices. Experts exchanged experiences on immunization programs, vaccination at primary care and school levels, digitalization, pharmacovigilance, and vaccine procurement planning.

item.title: Central Asian Nations to Enhance Protection of Wetlands and Biodiversity
item.description: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan plan to expand cooperation in conserving wetlands and protecting biodiversity. This was discussed at the annual meeting of the Ramsar Regional Initiative for Central Asia in Astana. The meeting resulted in the Korgalzhyn Resolution, outlining joint priorities for 2026-2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Receive €104 Million for Climate Change Adaptation
item.description: Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan will receive €264.4 million in total for climate change adaptation, with Uzbekistan allocated €103.7 million. The initiative, supported by international partners, aims to restore forests and pastures, promote sustainable agriculture, and enhance the adaptive capacity of rural populations. The launch was announced at the World Climate Summit in Antalya.

item.title: COP31 Summit in Antalya Discusses Global Environmental Issues and Economic Development
item.description: The 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya is a platform for discussing global environmental problems in conjunction with economic development and human well-being. The summit addresses climate commitments, environmental risks, and promotes international cooperation for green development goals. Uzbekistan's environmental initiatives and opportunities are also being highlighted.

item.title: Uzbekistan Amends Extremism Law, Removes 'Religious Extremism' Definition
item.description: Uzbekistan has redefined 'extremism' in its laws, removing the specific term 'religious extremism' which had been criticized for restricting the rights of religious individuals. While the law has been amended, human rights advocates warn that restrictions on religious freedom and potential abuses may persist.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Early Detection Rate for Childhood Cancer to 28%
item.description: Uzbekistan has seen a rise in the early detection of childhood cancer, increasing from 23% in 2023 to 28% in 2025. The time from symptom suspicion to specialized treatment has significantly decreased. This progress is attributed to the 'Green Corridor' system and digital 'One Child - One Route' initiative.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Build New 150 MW Wind Farm with Halyk Bank and BRK Support
item.description: A new 150 MW wind farm, 'Zhuzimdik', will be constructed in the Turkestan region of Kazakhstan. A trilateral financing agreement was signed at the COP31 climate conference, involving Kazakhstan Utility Systems (KKS), Halyk Bank, and the Development Bank of Kazakhstan (BRK). Construction is slated to begin in March 2027.

item.title: US Deputy Secretary of State meets Kazakhstan's Special Representative in Washington
item.description: US Deputy Secretary of State Sarah Rogers met with Kazakhstan's Special Representative to international organizations, Yerzhan Kazykhan, in Washington. They discussed improving bilateral relations and the importance of a free press. Kazykhan was in Washington for the B20 USA Summit, engaging in constructive discussions on strategic partnership, education, and cultural cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov attends CSTO Collective Security Council session in Moscow
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrived at the Grand Kremlin Palace in Moscow to participate in the Collective Security Council session of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). Russian President Vladimir Putin welcomed the leaders. The meeting included heads of state from Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan, along with the CSTO Secretary General.

item.title: Andijan officials arrested for demanding $100,000 bribe for land allocation
item.description: An Andijan regional governor's deputy and a cadastral employee have been arrested for demanding a $100,000 bribe. They allegedly promised to help a businessman acquire 50 sotok (0.5 hectares) of land at a low price through an auction. The officials were apprehended while receiving $30,000 of the demanded sum.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Require Advance Applications for Currency Purchases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARFR) is introducing new rules for large foreign currency purchases. Non-residents will face stricter controls, including biometrics, for opening brokerage accounts. Transactions exceeding $3 million for individuals and $10 million for legal entities will require advance applications at least one business day prior.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Fined Six Banks and Two MFIs in October
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank imposed fines on six banks and two microfinance organizations (MFIs) in October for non-compliance with legislation and prudential norms. The Banking Supervision Committee reviewed 43 issues, including registration procedures and financial conditions of credit institutions. One bank and one MFI received warnings.

item.title: Around 20 Bangladeshi Citizens Recruited by Russia Killed in Ukraine
item.description: Approximately 20 Bangladeshi citizens recruited by the Russian army have been killed in the war in Ukraine. Most of them had no prior military training. The report comes amid an investigation into the death of Amir Kunakov in Al-Archa Gorge, leading to the dismissal of three officials from the Ministry of Emergency Situations.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Trade and Economic Ties with Bangladesh Prime Minister
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on the sidelines of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya. They discussed prospects for developing bilateral relations, noting positive dynamics in contacts and trade growth. Both sides agreed to enhance political dialogue, economic partnership, and industrial cooperation.
